part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then they rowed away, the songs say, along the Mysian shore, and past the mouth of Rhindacus, till they found a pleasant bay, sheltered by the long ridges of Arganthus, and by high walls of basalt rock.  And there they ran the ship ashore upon the yellow sand, and furled the sail, and took the mast down, and lashed it in its crutch.  And next they let down the ladder, and went ashore to sport and rest.

translation.en: The songs say they rowed along the Mysian shore and past the mouth of the Rhindacus.
translation.kr: 전설에 따르면, 그들은 미시아 해안을 따라 린다코스 강어귀를 지나 노를 저어갔습니다.

translation.en: They eventually found a pleasant bay sheltered by the long ridges of Arganthus and high walls of basalt rock.
translation.kr: 마침내 그들은 아르간토스의 긴 능선과 높은 현무암 절벽으로 둘러싸인 아늑한 만을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They ran the ship ashore onto the yellow sand, furled the sail, and took down the mast to lash it in its crutch.
translation.kr: 그들은 노란 모래사장에 배를 대고 돛을 접은 뒤, 돛대를 내려 받침대에 단단히 묶었습니다.

translation.en: Next, they let down the ladder and went ashore to rest and play.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 사다리를 내리고 뭍으로 올라가 휴식을 취하며 즐거운 시간을 보냈습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: And there Heracles went away into the woods, bow in hand, to hunt wild deer; and Hylas the fair boy slipt away after him, and followed him by stealth, until he lost himself among the glens, and sat down weary to rest himself by the side of a lake; and there the water nymphs came up to look at him, and loved him, and carried him down under the lake to be their playfellow, for ever happy and young.  And Heracles sought for him in vain, shouting his name till all the mountains rang; but Hylas never heard him, far down under the sparkling lake.  So while Heracles wandered searching for him, a fair breeze sprang up, and Heracles was nowhere to be found; and the _Argo_ sailed away, and Heracles was left behind, and never saw the noble Phasian stream.

translation.en: Heracles went into the woods with his bow to hunt wild deer.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 야생 사슴을 사냥하기 위해 활을 들고 숲으로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: The beautiful boy Hylas slipped away and stealthily followed him.
translation.kr: 아름다운 소년 힐라스가 남몰래 빠져나와 그의 뒤를 쫓았습니다.

translation.en: Hylas soon lost his way among the glens and sat down wearily by a lake to rest.
translation.kr: 곧 골짜기에서 길을 잃은 힐라스는 지친 몸을 이끌고 호숫가에 주저앉아 쉬었습니다.

translation.en: The water nymphs came up to look at him and instantly fell in love.
translation.kr: 물의 요정들이 그를 보러 수면 위로 올라왔다가 첫눈에 반하고 말았습니다.

translation.en: They carried him down beneath the lake to be their playmate, forever happy and young.
translation.kr: 그들은 영원히 젊고 행복하게 함께 놀기 위해 소년을 호수 밑바닥으로 데려갔습니다.

translation.en: Heracles searched for him in vain, shouting his name until the mountains rang.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스는 산이 쩌렁쩌렁 울리도록 소년의 이름을 부르며 찾아 헤매었으나 헛수고였습니다.

translation.en: Far down under the sparkling lake, Hylas never heard his calls.
translation.kr: 반짝이는 호수 저 깊은 곳에 있는 힐라스에게는 그 목소리가 닿지 않았습니다.

translation.en: While Heracles wandered in search of the boy, a fair breeze sprang up.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스가 소년을 찾아 헤매는 동안 순조로운 바람이 불기 시작했습니다.

translation.en: When Heracles could not be found, the Argo sailed away without him.
translation.kr: 헤라클레스가 끝내 돌아오지 않자, 아르고 호는 그를 남겨둔 채 출항해 버렸습니다.

translation.en: Thus, Heracles was left behind and never saw the noble Phasis River.
translation.kr: 결국 홀로 남겨진 헤라클레스는 그 장엄한 파시스 강을 영영 보지 못했습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then the Minuai came to a doleful land, where Amycus the giant ruled, and cared nothing for the laws of Zeus, but challenged all strangers to box with him, and those whom he conquered he slew.  But Polydeuces the boxer struck him a harder blow than he ever felt before, and slew him; and the Minuai went on up the Bosphorus, till they came to the city of Phineus, the fierce Bithynian king; for Zetes and Calais bade Jason land there, because they had a work to do.

translation.en: The Minyans then arrived at a mournful land ruled by the giant Amycus.
translation.kr: 그 후 미니아이 사람들은 거인 아미코스가 지배하는 음울한 땅에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He cared nothing for the laws of Zeus and challenged all strangers to a boxing match, slaying those he defeated.
translation.kr: 그는 제우스의 법칙을 무시한 채 낯선 이들에게 권투 시합을 걸어 패자들을 모조리 죽여버렸습니다.

translation.en: However, the expert boxer Polydeuces struck the giant with a crushing blow and killed him.
translation.kr: 하지만 뛰어난 권투 선수 폴리데우케스가 뼈가 부서질 듯한 강력한 일격을 날려 거인을 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: The Argonauts continued up the Bosphorus until they reached the city of Phineus, the fierce Bithynian king.
translation.kr: 아르고 호 원정대는 보스포루스 해협을 거슬러 올라가 맹렬한 비티니아의 왕 피네우스의 도시에 닿았습니다.

translation.en: Zetes and Calais had urged Jason to land there because they had a task to fulfill.
translation.kr: 제테스와 칼라이스는 자신들이 완수해야 할 임무가 있다며 이아손에게 그곳에 상륙하자고 재촉했습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: And they went up from the shore toward the city, through forests white with snow; and Phineus came out to meet them with a lean and woful face, and said, ‘Welcome, gallant heroes, to the land of bitter blasts, the land of cold and misery; yet I will feast you as best I can.’  And he led them in, and set meat before them; but before they could put their hands to their mouths, down came two fearful monsters, the like of whom man never saw; for they had the faces and the hair of fair maidens, but the wings and claws of hawks; and they snatched the meat from off the table, and flew shrieking out above the roofs.

translation.en: They walked from the shore toward the city through forests white with snow.
translation.kr: 그들은 해안에서 출발해 눈 덮인 하얀 숲을 지나 도시를 향해 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: Phineus came out to meet them with a gaunt and sorrowful face.
translation.kr: 피네우스가 수척하고 슬픈 얼굴로 나와 그들을 맞이했습니다.

translation.en: Welcome, gallant heroes, to the land of bitter blasts, cold, and misery, he said.
translation.kr: 용감한 영웅들이여, 살을 에는 듯한 칼바람과 추위, 그리고 고통의 땅에 오신 것을 환영합니다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: Yet I will feast you as best as I can.
translation.kr: 하지만 최선을 다해 여러분을 대접하겠습니다.

translation.en: He led them inside and set meat before them on the table.
translation.kr: 왕은 그들을 안으로 안내하여 고기를 식탁에 차려주었습니다.

translation.en: But before they could take a single bite, two fearful monsters swooped down.
translation.kr: 그러나 그들이 한 입 베어 물기도 전에 끔찍한 두 괴물이 쏜살같이 내려왔습니다.

translation.en: These creatures had the faces and hair of fair maidens, but the wings and claws of hawks.
translation.kr: 그 생물들은 아름다운 처녀의 얼굴과 머리카락을 가졌지만, 매의 날개와 발톱을 하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They snatched the meat from the table and flew shrieking away above the roofs.
translation.kr: 괴물들은 식탁에서 고기를 낚아채더니 날카로운 비명을 지르며 지붕 위로 날아가 버렸습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then Phineus beat his breast and cried, ‘These are the Harpies, whose names are the Whirlwind and the Swift, the daughters of Wonder and of the Amber-nymph, and they rob us night and day.  They carried off the daughters of Pandareus, whom all the Gods had blest; for Aphrodite fed them on Olympus with honey and milk and wine; and Hera gave them beauty and wisdom, and Athené skill in all the arts; but when they came to their wedding, the Harpies snatched them both away, and gave them to be slaves to the Erinnues, and live in horror all their days.  And now they haunt me, and my people, and the Bosphorus, with fearful storms; and sweep away our food from off our tables, so that we starve in spite of all our wealth.’

translation.en: Phineus beat his chest in despair and cried out.
translation.kr: 피네우스는 절망에 빠져 가슴을 치며 울부짖었습니다.

translation.en: These are the Harpies, the daughters of Wonder and the Amber-nymph.
translation.kr: 이들은 경이로움의 신과 호박의 요정 사이에서 태어난 딸들, 바로 하르피이아이입니다.

translation.en: Their names are Whirlwind and Swift, and they rob us night and day.
translation.kr: 돌풍과 발빠름이라는 이름을 가진 이 괴물들은 밤낮을 가리지 않고 우리를 약탈합니다.

translation.en: They once carried off the blessed daughters of Pandareus.
translation.kr: 그들은 과거에 신들의 축복을 받은 판다레오스의 딸들도 납치해 갔습니다.

translation.en: Aphrodite had fed those girls on Olympus with honey, milk, and wine.
translation.kr: 아프로디테는 올림포스에서 그 소녀들에게 꿀과 우유, 포도주를 먹여 키웠습니다.

translation.en: Hera gave them beauty and wisdom, while Athena taught them skill in all the arts.
translation.kr: 헤라는 아름다움과 지혜를, 아테나는 모든 예술의 재능을 주었습니다.

translation.en: But on their wedding day, the Harpies snatched them away to be slaves to the Furies.
translation.kr: 그러나 결혼식 날, 하르피이아이가 신부들을 낚아채 복수의 여신들의 노예로 만들어 버렸습니다.

translation.en: The poor girls were forced to live in horror for the rest of their days.
translation.kr: 가엾은 소녀들은 평생을 끔찍한 공포 속에서 살아야만 했습니다.

translation.en: Now they haunt me, my people, and the Bosphorus with fearful storms.
translation.kr: 이제 그 괴물들은 무서운 폭풍우를 몰고 와 저와 제 백성, 그리고 보스포루스 해협을 끈질기게 괴롭힙니다.

translation.en: They sweep the food from our tables, leaving us to starve despite all our wealth.
translation.kr: 그들은 우리 식탁의 음식마저 모조리 휩쓸어 가버려서, 우리는 아무리 부유해도 굶주려야만 합니다.
